'''Earl Alexander Coddington''' (1920–1991) was an American mathematician and professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) and an author whose textbook on differential equations, written jointly with [[Norman Levinson]] is considered a classic and is used in universities all over the world.{{citation needed|date=June 2017}}

== Life ==

He was born on December 16, 1920, in Washington, DC.<ref name="Death">{{citation|title=Earl A. Coddington|quote=Earl A. Coddington. Born 16 Dec 1920, Died 11 Nov 1991, Social Security Card issued before 1951 in District of Columbia|work=Social Security Death Index, Master File. Social Security Administration}}</ref><ref name="CA Death">{{citation|title=Earl A. Coddington|work=State of California. California Death Index, 1940–1997. Sacramento, CA, USA: State of California Department of Health Services, Center for Health Statistics}}</ref> From the [[Johns Hopkins University]], he received a PhD<ref name="Princeton">{{cite book|title=Princeton Alumni Weekly|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UxJbAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA12|year=1957|publisher=Princeton Alumni Weekly|page=12|chapter=Visiting Scholars – Mathematics|id=PRNC:32101081976928}}</ref> in 1948. His dissertation was ''On the Equations Governing the Stability of the Laminar Boundary Layer in a Compressible Fluid.''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jscholarship.library.jhu.edu/bitstream/handle/1774.2/36790/commencement1948.pdf|title=Conferring of Degrees At the Close of the Seventy-Second Academic Year|date=June 8, 1948|publisher=The Johns Hopkins University|accessdate=June 19, 2017}}</ref>

He died on November 11, 1991, in Los Angeles, California.<ref name="Death" /><ref name="CA Death" />

== Career ==
He was a professor of mathematics at UCLA.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/166016722/?terms=Earl%2BCoddington%2BUCLA |title=Civil Liberties Union to Sponsor Forum|date=March 12, 1967 |newspaper=The Los Angeles Times|page=585|accessdate=June 19, 2017|via=newspapers.com|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Trombley">{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/164195165/?terms=Earl%2BCoddington%2BUCLA |title=Professors Taking Up Battle Against Reagan | author=William Trombley |date=May 15, 1967 |newspaper=The Los Angeles Times|page=113|accessdate=June 19, 2017|via=newspapers.com|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He came to the department about 1950, as did other professors who helped to build the department into one of the top university mathematics departments. Others who arrived about that time that also helped to build the department were [[Raymond Redheffer]], [[Ernst Straus]], [[Robert Steinberg]], [[Richard Arens]], and Philip Curtis.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/_files/inmemoriam/html/raymondredheffer.htm|title=Raymond Redheffer|website=Senate, University of California|accessdate=June 19, 2017}}</ref> He was also a leader of the Citizens for California Higher Education the chair of the American Association of University Professors for the campus. He organized against Governor [[Ronald Reagan]]'s plan to reduce spending to universities and increase tuition.<ref name="Trombley" />

Coddington was a visiting scholar at [[Princeton University]] and taught at the [[University of Copenhagen]] and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="Princeton" /> He frequently collaborated with Norman Levinson. His textbook on differential equations written with Levinson (colloquially referred to as ''Coddington–Levinson'') is now considered a classic and is used in universities all over the world.
